Bug_Details:
Serialization is a platform-independent mechanism for writing the state of an object into a byte-stream. For serializing the object, we call the writeObject() method of java.io.ObjectOutputStream class. Only classes that implement Serializable or extend a
class that does it can successfully be serialized (or de-serialized).
Attempting to write a class with the writeObject method of the ObjectOutputStream class that does not implement Serializable or extends a class that implements it, will throw an IOException .
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by attempting to serialize an instance of NonSerializableClass, which does not implement the Serializable interface. This results in an IOException being thrown when the writeObject method of ObjectOutputStream is called.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the showBug method of SerializationBugExample, which attempts to serialize an instance of NonSerializableClass using ObjectOutputStream.writeObject(). Since NonSerializableClass does not implement Serializable, this triggers an IOException, causing the test to fail.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test run results indicate that the test passed without throwing any exceptions, which means the bug was not triggered during the test execution.
